threshold_note: Unstable Rift calls (crates/engine/src/rift.rs, docs/rift.md). Times are wiki facts (docs/strategy/midgame-macro.md section 8: effect -> 60 s -> announcement -> 20 s -> open; first effect 10-12 min, later ones 6-8 min after the previous). Team counts need all twelve top-bar slots read (TeamPicture). 'behind_pct': our team souls this far under theirs (the wiki's comeback bonus is linear up to 15%). 'skip_dead': this many of us dead (you alive), and more of us than of them, skips it. Contest: the wiki's warning shows after 50 s, the draw at 60 s; the coach counts only the contest it saw. Priorities: the announcement call (go / behind / skip), 'stop' and 'draw' are timed (20 s to the opening, a 12 s capture, the 60 s draw) and speak as High (in a fight cut to their first clause); the after-calls are Normal with half the phase gap (lib.rs). No go / stop call under 'min_hp' health; with the lane not read yet the announcement call waits until 'lane_wait_secs' before the opening.

cards.speech: Rift soon, from {time} on a side-lane bridge: push your wave first.
cards.rationale: The Rift is announced at a known window; arriving with your wave pushed means you lose no farm and your lane is not under your Guardian while you fight.

sources.excerpt: meaning the first Rift can spawn at any time between 10 and 12 minutes, and subsequent Rifts can spawn between 6 and 8 minutes after the previous Rift
Before any group objective: check which teammates are near, ults ready, waves cleared

cards.speech: Rift {where} in {secs} seconds: {up} group {with}on the bridge.
variants: The Rift is open {where}: {up} group {with}on the bridge.
cards.rationale: It opens 20 s after the announcement and only a team alone in the point claims it: arriving together is what takes it.

sources.excerpt: 20 seconds after the announcement, the Rift opens and creates a capture point with a 20m radius around the bridge
but the Rift can only be claimed once there's only one team in the point

cards.speech: We're behind, so we capture the Rift faster: all go {where_short}.
cards.rationale: The trailing team captures in as little as 6 s and fights inside a resist aura: the Rift is the comeback objective.

sources.excerpt: Capture time reduced to 6s (50% shorter) for the trailing team, and increased to 18s (50% longer) for the leading team.
Bonus Bullet, Spirit, and Debuff Resist, provided within a 35m radius.

cards.rationale: Both teams progress while both are in the point and only a lone team claims it: with fewer of us alive we cannot hold it, and a lost fight costs more than the bounty.

sources.excerpt: Both teams earn progress as long as they have at least one player in the capture point
losing a 5v6 costs more than a camp

cards.speech: They're alone on the Rift: step in to stop the capture.
cards.rationale: A single player of ours in the point stops their claim (it needs one team alone), and progress does not depend on how many are in.

sources.excerpt: The progress rate is the same regardless of how many players per team are in the point.
but the Rift can only be claimed once there's only one team in the point

cards.speech: The Rift draws in {secs} seconds: grab the soul orbs.
variants: The Rift is a draw: grab the soul orbs.
cards.rationale: After 60 s contested the souls drop as orbs either team can take; standing on them is the reward.

sources.excerpt: After 60s of being contested, the Rift ends in a draw. No Rift Troopers are spawned, and all souls are released as 13 Soul Orbs to be claimed by either team.

cards.rationale: Our Rift Troopers have double health and damage and resist melee: they tank the next structure if heroes walk behind them.

sources.excerpt: Rift Troopers will spawn in that lane for the winning team.
On the first rift, they have +100% health and damage compared to normal troopers

cards.speech: Their Rift Troopers are coming down {where_short}: defend at the Guardian, don't fight them alone.
cards.rationale: Their Rift Troopers have double health and damage, resist melee and give no souls: meet them with your wave at the Guardian.

sources.excerpt: They are larger, colored black, and don't drop souls when killed.
On the first rift, they have +100% health and damage compared to normal troopers, as well as 25% Melee Resist, and 30% Spirit Resist.
